newsitem.title: SPAIN: Endesa purchase raises questions on transparency.
newsitem.headline: Endesa purchase raises questions on transparency.

text.p: Spanish electricity firm Endesa's friendly buy offer for two regional firms has rekindled the smouldering issue of market transparency as traders ask why it told the bourse authority its plans only at the last minute.

The stock market commission CNMV would neither confirm or deny on Thursday press reports that it was investigating bourse movements preceding Endesa's announcement that it was taking control of Fecsa and Sevillana.
"For the moment I can't confirm anything," a CNMV spokeswoman said. "I can neither confirm nor deny it."
The state-owned electricity firm on Friday announced it would buy up to 75 percent of Fecsa and Sevillana, confirming the essence of a newspaper report published eight days earlier.
The CNMV briefly suspended trading in the shares ahead of a statement by the Industry Ministry.

Madrid traders privately commented on their surprise that both the ministry and Endesa had appeared to ignore the CNMV by not informing it of their plans until the night before the public announcement. But none were prepared to be quoted on the sensitive issue of market transparency.
